overview: The Wookiee clans of Kashyyyk are a proud, honor-bound civilization living in the wroshyr forests of their homeworld. Governed by the Wookiee Council, they maintained a sophisticated tree-city society for millennia before Imperial enslavement. During the Imperial era, Kashyyyk is one of the most heavily patrolled enslaved worlds in the galaxy, and free Wookiees are fugitives by definition — many channeling their rage and loyalty into the Rebel Alliance or independent resistance.
short_descriptor: Loyal beyond what the Empire understands, which is why the Empire underestimated them. If you have standing with a Wookiee clan, treat it carefully. That relationship will outlast the current conflict.

witness_statement.text: I brokered timber rights on Kashyyyk for six seasons before the Empire moved in. The day they came for the clans, a Wookiee I'd traded with for years pulled me behind a wroshyr root and held me there until the stormtroopers passed. Didn't say a word. Didn't have to. I owed him my life and he never once mentioned it. That's how they are — they remember everything and they never make it transactional.
witness_statement.source: Former trade delegate, Mytaranor Sector — voluntary deposition

how_they_operate.heading: CLANS AND COUNCIL
how_they_operate.text: Wookiee society is organized into clans, each led by a chieftain, with inter-clan coordination handled by the Wookiee Council on Kashyyyk. Before Imperial occupation, the Council governed a population of approximately 56 million across the wroshyr tree-cities of the Mid Rim world.

how_they_operate.heading: RESISTANCE
how_they_operate.text: Under the Empire, resistance operates through decentralized clan-based guerrilla cells in the wroshyr forest canopy and lower levels, coordinating via Shyriiwook calls, physical runners, and limited comlink networks the Empire attempts to jam.

how_they_operate.heading: LIFE DEBTS
how_they_operate.text: Life debts — permanent, unconditional obligations of loyalty — bind individual Wookiees to those who save them, creating bonds that function as an unbreakable command structure in the field.

how_they_operate.heading: ARMS AND WARRIORS
how_they_operate.text: Clan warriors fight with hand-crafted bowcasters, Ryyk blades marked with their city of origin, and Auzituck-class gunships produced by Appazanna Engineering Works for space interdiction against slaver vessels.

motivations.primary: Liberation of Kashyyyk and the Wookiee people
secondary: Preservation of clan honor and family bonds
Vengeance against the Empire and Trandoshan slavers
Protection of the wroshyr forest ecology that defines their civilization
Fulfillment of life debts and honor obligations
motivations.notes: Wookiee motivations are intensely personal and clan-based. The liberation of Kashyyyk is the overarching goal, but individual Wookiees are driven by specific family bonds, life debts, and honor codes. A Wookiee's loyalty to those they have sworn to protect is absolute and permanent.

strategic: Free Kashyyyk from Imperial occupation and dismantle the slave-processing infrastructure
Destroy the Trandoshan Slavers Guild operations on Trandosha and Alaris Prime
Restore the Wookiee Council as the governing authority of Kashyyyk
Ensure the long-term survival of wroshyr forest ecology against Imperial industrial exploitation
operational: Rescue enslaved Wookiees from Imperial labor projects and Trandoshan hunting reserves
Maintain covert resistance cells in the wroshyr forests despite heavy Imperial patrols
Smuggle weapons and supplies to resistance fighters on Kashyyyk
Build alliances with the Rebel Alliance and sympathetic smugglers for logistical support

avoided: Dishonorable tactics — Wookiees follow strict codes of honor even in war
Abandoning family or clan members regardless of tactical cost
Using the lower levels of Kashyyyk's forests as a weapon against enemies who don't understand them — though some desperate clans break this taboo
methods.notes: Wookiees fight with ferocity but within an honor framework. Their intimate knowledge of wroshyr forest ecology gives them enormous tactical advantages on Kashyyyk. Traditional weapons like bowcasters and Ryyk blades are preferred alongside modern blasters. Clan warriors coordinate through deep family bonds rather than formal military hierarchy.

strengths: Extraordinary physical strength and endurance — Wookiees are among the most physically powerful sentient species in the galaxy
Intimate knowledge of Kashyyyk's wroshyr forest ecology, including the lethal lower levels that terrify even Wookiees
Unbreakable loyalty bonds — life debts and clan honor create fighters who will never abandon allies
Sophisticated engineering tradition including the Auzituck gunship and hand-crafted bowcasters
Generational resistance experience — Wookiees have been fighting Imperial slavery since the end of the Clone Wars
weaknesses: The clan-based organizational structure lacks a unified command hierarchy, preventing coordinated military action across multiple Wookiee resistance groups simultaneously.
Life debts and family bonds create predictable pressure points that Imperial forces exploit through hostage-taking and targeted detention of clan members.
Free Wookiees carry Imperial fugitive status galaxy-wide, severely restricting their ability to travel, resupply, or establish logistics networks outside sympathetic enclaves.
The deep ancestral enmity between Wookiees and Trandoshans produces predictable emotional responses that adversaries can use to draw Wookiee fighters into unfavorable engagements.
Prolonged enslavement has produced internal divisions within clans between active resistance advocates and those who prioritize survival through compliance, weakening collective decision-making.

behavior_under_threat.low: Clan elders assess the threat through traditional council methods. Warriors maintain defensive positions in the wroshyr canopy.
behavior_under_threat.medium: Active guerrilla resistance mobilizes. Ambushes are set along forest paths. Allied smugglers are contacted for weapons resupply.
behavior_under_threat.high: Full clan mobilization. The deep forest becomes a killing ground. Life debts are called in. Auzituck gunships launch interdiction patrols against slaver vessels.
behavior_under_threat.critical: Total war posture. Clans that normally operate independently coordinate through the Wookiee Council. Even the dangerous lower forest levels become part of the defense. No retreat — Kashyyyk is everything.

chain_of_command: Clan scouts and sentries in the wroshyr canopy
Allied Rebel Alliance contacts (for off-world threats)
alert_escalation.notes: Communication within the forest uses a combination of Shyriiwook calls, physical messenger runners, and limited comlink networks that the Empire attempts to jam. Inter-clan coordination is slow due to the decentralized structure but becomes remarkably effective once the Council issues a unified call.

tension_patterns: Generational divisions within clans consistently emerge between elders who advocate traditional guerrilla methods and younger warriors who favor direct confrontation with Imperial forces.
Escaped slaves returning to Kashyyyk frequently carry valuable intelligence about Imperial operations but also draw Trandoshan bounty hunters and Imperial tracking teams to the clan's location.

Resistance supply networks in the Outer Rim often service multiple clients including Trandoshan operations, creating dependencies where severing a hostile supply line simultaneously disrupts the clan's own logistics.
Imperial forces routinely use Wookiee hostages as leverage against clan action, and rescue operations carry inherent risk of hostage casualties that compounds the original strategic constraint.

Wookiees who accept Imperial resettlement programs to protect their families occupy an ambiguous status within clan honor codes, dividing communities between those who view compliance as collaboration and those who recognize it as survival.

mcguffin_interest.notes: Wookiee clans prioritize weapons for the resistance and the recovery of enslaved persons above all else. Data about Imperial slave operations and patrol schedules is highly valued. Technology that supports the resistance is welcome. Ancient Wookiee artifacts have cultural significance but are not operational priorities.

relationship_notes.rebel_alliance: Natural allies — enslaved Wookiees who escape Imperial captivity frequently join the Alliance, and Rebel operations have targeted Wookiee slave camps.
relationship_notes.imperial_military: The primary oppressor — the Empire enslaved Kashyyyk en masse and heavily patrols the world and its surrounding space.
relationship_notes.imperial_security_bureau: ISB oversees the political suppression of Wookiee resistance and coordinates intelligence against resistance cells.
relationship_notes.hutt_cartel: Complicated — some Hutts employ Wookiee gladiators and participate in the slave trade, while individual smugglers under Hutt patronage sometimes aid the resistance.
relationship_notes.bounty_hunters_guild: Hostile in practice — bounty hunters frequently pursue escaped Wookiee slaves for Imperial bounties.

prominent_figures.name: Lowhhrick
prominent_figures.role: Example Wookiee hired gun (EotE sample character)
prominent_figures.notes: A surly Wookiee hired gun used as a sample character throughout the EotE Core Rulebook. Represents the common archetype of a free Wookiee working on the Fringe while carrying the weight of his people's enslavement.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Freelance muscle on the Fringe. No command authority within clan structures, but his contacts among free Wookiees make him a potential intermediary for anyone trying to reach the resistance.
prominent_figures.wants: Work that pays and doesn't require him to think too hard about the enslaved Wookiees he can't help. Takes dangerous jobs because the alternative is sitting still with his guilt.
prominent_figures.secret: He knows the location of at least one clan resistance cell on Kashyyyk and deliberately avoids returning because he believes his Imperial fugitive status would draw trackers to them.

behavior.under_pressure: Violence. Lowhhrick's first and preferred response to any threat is overwhelming physical force. De-escalation is not in his vocabulary.
behavior.when_losing: Fights harder. A Wookiee's response to being outmatched is to become more dangerous, not less. Retreat requires someone else to physically drag him out.
behavior.loyalty: Life debts and personal bonds. Once Lowhhrick commits to someone, that commitment is permanent and unconditional regardless of circumstances.
behavior.tells: His temper is the tell. When he goes quiet instead of angry, something has genuinely frightened him — and very few things frighten a Wookiee.

useful_to_players: His connections to free Wookiees on the Fringe provide access to a network of experienced fighters and resistance contacts
His guilt about Kashyyyk is a leverage point — a credible plan to help enslaved Wookiees would secure his total commitment
He is straightforward and honest to a fault, making him a reliable partner in situations where Bothan-style misdirection would be counterproductive
hooks: Lowhhrick turned down a well-paying bodyguard gig on Nar Shaddaa last week. That's not like him. Somebody mentioned Trandoshans were involved and he went silent. There's a story there.

A smuggler on the Kwenn Station run says Lowhhrick's been asking about slave transport schedules in the Mytaranor sector. He's not planning a rescue — he doesn't have the resources. He's looking for someone specific.

prominent_figures.name: Tarfful
prominent_figures.role: Wookiee military leader during the Clone Wars
prominent_figures.notes: Wookiee chieftain who fought alongside Republic forces during the Battle of Kashyyyk in the Clone Wars. Status during Imperial occupation is uncertain but he represents the warrior-chieftain tradition of Wookiee leadership.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: If alive, he is the highest-ranking Wookiee military leader with Clone Wars combat experience. His survival would be a significant morale asset for the resistance. His status is the most valuable unknown in Kashyyyk intelligence.
prominent_figures.wants: The liberation of Kashyyyk and the restoration of Wookiee self-governance under the Council. Every other consideration is secondary to the survival and freedom of his people.
prominent_figures.secret: His Clone Wars experience includes working directly with Republic military intelligence. If he survived the Imperial occupation, he possesses operational knowledge of Republic-era military infrastructure on Kashyyyk that the Empire may not have fully mapped.

behavior.under_pressure: Commands. Tarfful's response to threat is to organize — assign defensive positions, coordinate clan warriors, and establish communication with allied forces. He is a military leader, not a berserker.
behavior.when_losing: Retreats to the deep forest and regroups. Tarfful survived the Clone Wars and the Imperial occupation by knowing when to withdraw into terrain the enemy cannot follow.
behavior.loyalty: Kashyyyk and its people. Tarfful's loyalty is to the Wookiee species as a whole, transcending individual clan boundaries — a rare quality that makes him a unifying figure.
behavior.tells: When Tarfful stops communicating through intermediaries and appears in person, the situation has reached a level of severity that demands unified clan action.

useful_to_players: His Clone Wars contacts may include surviving Republic officers now embedded in the Rebel Alliance command structure
His authority transcends clan boundaries, making him the only figure who could coordinate a multi-clan operation on Kashyyyk
Confirming his survival or death would be a high-value intelligence product for both the Rebellion and the Empire
hooks: A Wookiee escaped from an Imperial labor camp on Kessel claims to have seen a chieftain organizing prisoners — descriptions match Tarfful but the source is unreliable and traumatized. Confirming the sighting is worth a trip to Kessel if you can stomach it.

An old Republic military frequency in the Kashyyyk system started transmitting coded bursts last month. The encryption is Clone Wars era. Either someone found old equipment, or someone who knows Clone Wars protocols is alive and signaling.

source_material_notes: Wookiees receive extensive species treatment in EotE Core pp.61-62 and cultural/planetary coverage in Collapse of the Republic pp.112-113 (Kashyyyk profile). AoR Core pp.45, 363, 372 covers their enslavement and resistance. FaD Core pp.361-362 describes Kashyyyk's deep Force connection. Equipment and ship references appear across multiple sourcebooks. The Soldier Sourcebook p.15 specifically references Wookiee resistance fighters as a Trailblazer archetype.
